RQ4: How can we accurately estimate energy consumption before training DL models for image classification?

Santiago del Rey

Load data

df <- read_parquet("data/metrics/processed/clean-dl-training-energy-consumption-dataset.gzip") %>%
  rename(
    energy = `energy (MJ)`,
    power_draw = `average gpu power (W)`,
    training_duration = `training duration (h)`,
    used_ram = `average ram used (MB)`,
    batch_size = `batch size`,
    image_size = `image size`,
    allocated_ram = `total ram (GB)`,
    training_environment = `training environment`,
  ) %>%
  filter(architecture == "inception_v3") %>%
  mutate(
    energy_per_image = (energy * 1000000) / `total seen images`, # Convert MJ to J and normalize by total seen images
    training_duration = training_duration * 60, # Convert hours to minutes
    epoch_duration = training_duration / `trained epochs`, # Calculate average epoch duration in minutes
    batch_size = factor(batch_size, levels = c("32", "64", "256")),
    input_size = factor(image_size, levels = c("(75, 75)", "(128, 128)", "(224, 224)")),
    allocated_ram = factor(allocated_ram, levels = c("8", "16", "24", "32")),
    dataset = factor(dataset),
    dataset = case_match(
      dataset,
      "stanford_dogs" ~ "Stanford Dogs",
      "caltech101" ~ "Caltech 101"
    )
  ) %>%
  select(energy_per_image, power_draw, training_duration, epoch_duration, used_ram, batch_size, input_size, dataset, training_environment, allocated_ram)

Visualize the data

Data summary

df_batch_input <- df %>%
  filter(training_environment == "Server" & allocated_ram == 16) %>%
  group_by(batch_size, input_size, dataset) %>%
  mutate(
    Q1 = quantile(energy_per_image, 0.25),
    Q3 = quantile(energy_per_image, 0.75),
    IQR = Q3 - Q1,
    is_outlier = energy_per_image < (Q1 - 1.5 * IQR) | energy_per_image > (Q3 + 1.5 * IQR)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(!is_outlier) %>%
  select(-Q1, -Q3, -IQR, -is_outlier)

df_batch_input %>%
  group_by(batch_size, input_size, dataset) %>%
  get_summary_stats(energy_per_image, type = "mean_sd")
df_allocated_ram_energy <- df %>%
  filter(batch_size == "256" & input_size == "(128, 128)" & dataset == "Stanford Dogs" & training_environment == "Server") %>%
  group_by(allocated_ram) %>%
  mutate(
    Q1 = quantile(energy_per_image, 0.25),
    Q3 = quantile(energy_per_image, 0.75),
    IQR = Q3 - Q1,
    is_outlier = energy_per_image < (Q1 - 1.5 * IQR) | energy_per_image > (Q3 + 1.5 * IQR)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(!is_outlier) %>%
  select(-Q1, -Q3, -IQR, -is_outlier)

df_allocated_ram_energy %>%
  group_by(allocated_ram) %>%
  get_summary_stats(energy_per_image, type = "mean_sd")
df_allocated_ram_time <- df %>%
  filter(batch_size == "256" & input_size == "(128, 128)" & dataset == "Stanford Dogs" & training_environment == "Server") %>%
  group_by(allocated_ram) %>%
  mutate(
    Q1 = quantile(training_duration, 0.25),
    Q3 = quantile(training_duration, 0.75),
    IQR = Q3 - Q1,
    is_outlier = training_duration < (Q1 - 1.5 * IQR) | training_duration > (Q3 + 1.5 * IQR)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(!is_outlier) %>%
  select(-Q1, -Q3, -IQR, -is_outlier)
df_allocated_ram_time %>%
  group_by(allocated_ram) %>%
  get_summary_stats(training_duration, type = "mean_sd")
df_allocated_ram_ram <- df %>%
  filter(batch_size == "256" & input_size == "(128, 128)" & dataset == "Stanford Dogs" & training_environment == "Server") %>%
  group_by(allocated_ram) %>%
  mutate(
    Q1 = quantile(used_ram, 0.25),
    Q3 = quantile(used_ram, 0.75),
    IQR = Q3 - Q1,
    is_outlier = used_ram < (Q1 - 1.5 * IQR) | used_ram > (Q3 + 1.5 * IQR)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(!is_outlier) %>%
  select(-Q1, -Q3, -IQR, -is_outlier)
df_allocated_ram_ram %>%
  group_by(allocated_ram) %>%
  get_summary_stats(used_ram, type = "mean_sd")

Boxplot of energy consumption

energy_boxplot <- ggplot(df_batch_input, aes(x = input_size, y = energy_per_image, color = batch_size)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_wrap(~dataset) +
  labs(
    x = "Input Size",
    y = "Energy Consumption (J/image)",
    color = "Batch Size"
  )

plot(energy_boxplot)

ggsave(
  energy_boxplot + pub_theme,
  filename = file.path(fig_dir, "batch-and-input-size-effect-energy.pdf"),
  device = cairo_pdf,
  units = "cm",
  width = 13.71, height = 8, dpi = 300
)

Statistical analysis of the effects of batch size, input size, and dataset on energy consumption

Linear model with dataset as a fixed effect

model_lm <- lm(energy_per_image ~ batch_size * input_size * dataset, data = df_batch_input)
summary(model_lm)

Check assumptions of the linear model

sim_res <- simulateResiduals(model_lm)
testResiduals(sim_res)

## $uniformity
##
##  Asymptotic one-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test
##
## data:  simulationOutput$scaledResiduals
## D = 0.064231, p-value = 0.1523
## alternative hypothesis: two-sided
##
##
## $dispersion
##
##  DHARMa nonparametric dispersion test via sd of residuals fitted vs.
##  simulated
##
## data:  simulationOutput
## dispersion = 0.95288, p-value = 0.56
## alternative hypothesis: two.sided
##
##
## $outliers
##
##  DHARMa outlier test based on exact binomial test with approximate
##  expectations
##
## data:  simulationOutput
## outliers at both margin(s) = 3, observations = 312, p-value = 0.742
## alternative hypothesis: true probability of success is not equal to 0.007968127
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  0.00198733 0.02784156
## sample estimates:
## frequency of outliers (expected: 0.00796812749003984 )
##                                            0.009615385
check_model(model_lm)

Linear mixed model

model_lmm <- lmer(
  energy_per_image ~ batch_size * input_size + (1 | dataset),
  data = df_batch_input,
)
summary(model_lmm)

Generalized linear model with Gamma distribution

model_glm <- glm(
  energy_per_image ~ batch_size * input_size * dataset,
  data = df_batch_input,
  family = Gamma(link = "log")
)
summary(model_glm)
##

Compare models

Significance testing and effect size

options(contrasts = c("contr.sum", "contr.poly")) # sum-to-zero contrasts for Type III
Anova(model_lm) # Type III ANOVA for linear models
## Note: model has aliased coefficients
##       sums of squares computed by model comparison
eta_squared(model_lm, partial = FALSE) # Calculate eta squared for effect sizes
eta_squared(model_lm, partial = TRUE) # Partial eta squared for each term

Post hoc tests

Estimate the effect sizes of the fixed effects in the model.

# Tidy the model for plotting
tidy_lm <- broom::tidy(model_lm)

# Filter out intercept and sort by absolute effect size
tidy_lm_filtered <- tidy_lm[tidy_lm$term != "(Intercept)", ]
tidy_lm_filtered <- tidy_lm_filtered[order(abs(tidy_lm_filtered$estimate), decreasing = TRUE), ]
# Filter out terms with NA estimates
tidy_lm_filtered <- tidy_lm_filtered %>%
  filter(!is.na(estimate))

# Plot
eff_plot <- ggplot(tidy_lm_filtered, aes(x = reorder(term, abs(estimate)), y = estimate)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Effect Sizes",
    x = "Term",
    y = "Estimate (Energy Consumption Impact)"
  )

Estimate marginal means for the interaction between batch size and input size, conditioned on the dataset.

emm_lm <- emmeans(model_lm, ~ batch_size * input_size | dataset)
emm_lm

Plot the estimated marginal means.

emm_df <- as.data.frame(emm_lm) %>%
  filter(!is.na(emmean))

emm_plot <- ggplot(emm_df, aes(x = batch_size, y = emmean, group = input_size, color = input_size)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~dataset) +
  labs(
    title = "Estimated Marginal Means of Energy",
    x = "Batch Size",
    y = "Predicted Energy Consumption",
    color = "Input Size"
  )

combined_plot <- (eff_plot | emm_plot) +
  plot_annotation(title = "Energy Consumption Analysis", theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)))

combined_plot

Statistical analysis of the effects of allocated RAM on energy consumption

Linear model with allocated RAM as a fixed effect

model_lm_ram <- lm(energy_per_image ~ allocated_ram, data = df_allocated_ram_energy)
summary(model_lm_ram)
##
## Call:
## lm(formula = energy_per_image ~ allocated_ram, data = df_allocated_ram_energy)
##
## Residuals:
##        Min         1Q     Median         3Q        Max
## -8.867e-04 -2.572e-04 -2.338e-05  1.884e-04  1.041e-03
##
## Coefficients:
##                  Estimate Std. Error  t value Pr(>|t|)
## (Intercept)     5.582e-02  3.630e-05 1537.592  < 2e-16 ***
## allocated_ram1  4.169e-04  6.102e-05    6.832 5.83e-10 ***
## allocated_ram2  1.135e-04  6.811e-05    1.667   0.0985 .
## allocated_ram3 -7.732e-04  6.036e-05  -12.811  < 2e-16 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
##
## Residual standard error: 0.0003735 on 104 degrees of freedom
## Multiple R-squared:  0.6315, Adjusted R-squared:  0.6209
## F-statistic: 59.41 on 3 and 104 DF,  p-value: < 2.2e-16

Check assumptions of the linear model with allocated RAM

sim_res_ram <- simulateResiduals(model_lm_ram)
testResiduals(sim_res_ram)

## $uniformity
##
##  Asymptotic one-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test
##
## data:  simulationOutput$scaledResiduals
## D = 0.054444, p-value = 0.9061
## alternative hypothesis: two-sided
##
##
## $dispersion
##
##  DHARMa nonparametric dispersion test via sd of residuals fitted vs.
##  simulated
##
## data:  simulationOutput
## dispersion = 0.97017, p-value = 0.768
## alternative hypothesis: two.sided
##
##
## $outliers
##
##  DHARMa outlier test based on exact binomial test with approximate
##  expectations
##
## data:  simulationOutput
## outliers at both margin(s) = 2, observations = 108, p-value = 0.2129
## alternative hypothesis: true probability of success is not equal to 0.007968127
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  0.00225060 0.06529655
## sample estimates:
## frequency of outliers (expected: 0.00796812749003984 )
##                                             0.01851852
check_model(model_lm_ram)

Significance testing and effect size

Anova(model_lm_ram) # Type I ANOVA for linear models
eta_squared(model_lm_ram, partial = FALSE) # Calculate eta squared for effect sizes

Post hoc tests for allocated RAM

emm_ram <- emmeans(model_lm_ram, ~allocated_ram)
emm_ram
##  allocated_ram  emmean       SE  df lower.CL upper.CL
##  8             0.05623 6.94e-05 104  0.05610  0.05637
##  16            0.05593 8.15e-05 104  0.05577  0.05609
##  24            0.05504 6.82e-05 104  0.05491  0.05518
##  32            0.05606 7.06e-05 104  0.05592  0.05620
##
## Confidence level used: 0.95
pairs(emm_ram, adjust = "tukey")
##  contrast                           estimate       SE  df t.ratio p.value
##  allocated_ram8 - allocated_ram16   0.000303 1.07e-04 104   2.834  0.0278
##  allocated_ram8 - allocated_ram24   0.001190 9.73e-05 104  12.235  <.0001
##  allocated_ram8 - allocated_ram32   0.000174 9.90e-05 104   1.759  0.2990
##  allocated_ram16 - allocated_ram24  0.000887 1.06e-04 104   8.345  <.0001
##  allocated_ram16 - allocated_ram32 -0.000129 1.08e-04 104  -1.199  0.6290
##  allocated_ram24 - allocated_ram32 -0.001016 9.81e-05 104 -10.352  <.0001
##
## P value adjustment: tukey method for comparing a family of 4 estimates
eff_size(emm_ram, sigma = sigma(model_lm_ram), edf = df.residual(model_lm_ram))
##  contrast                          effect.size    SE  df lower.CL upper.CL
##  allocated_ram8 - allocated_ram16        0.812 0.292 104   0.2330    1.391
##  allocated_ram8 - allocated_ram24        3.186 0.342 104   2.5091    3.863
##  allocated_ram8 - allocated_ram32        0.466 0.267 104  -0.0633    0.995
##  allocated_ram16 - allocated_ram24       2.374 0.329 104   1.7224    3.026
##  allocated_ram16 - allocated_ram32      -0.346 0.290 104  -0.9205    0.228
##  allocated_ram24 - allocated_ram32      -2.720 0.323 104  -3.3617   -2.079
##
## sigma used for effect sizes: 0.0003735
## Confidence level used: 0.95
plot(emm_ram, comparisons = TRUE) +
  labs(
    title = "Estimated Marginal Means of Energy by Allocated RAM",
    x = "Predicted Energy Consumption (J/image)",
    y = "Allocated RAM (GB)",
  )
